need.title: Parse manifest data instead of substring-scanning it
need.what_is_missing_or_wrong: MCP and Ollama detection treats any occurrence of the words in raw manifest text as a positive signal, so comments, descriptions, or unrelated names containing those substrings can misclassify a repository.
need.what_done_would_look_like: Extract relevant dependency/configuration names from supported manifests and match exact normalized entries; add integration tests for legitimate entries and near-miss text such as comments or package names containing "mcp" or "ollama".
tree_evidence: gitseed/category.py:55-67 derive both manifest signals with `"mcp" in self._manifest(files)` and `"ollama" in self._manifest(files)`.
gitseed/category.py:78-83 concatenates raw text from several manifest formats rather than parsing their dependency/configuration structures.
tests/test_category.py:140-145 only asserts the built-in pack names; no test exercises manifest contents through `FileEvidenceReader`.
need.distinct_from_others_because: This concerns false positives in manifest-derived MCP/local-AI categories, independent of source scanning or incomplete fetch handling.

task_prompt:
Make manifest-based category evidence precise. For the supported manifest files (`package.json`, `pyproject.toml`, `Cargo.toml`, `go.mod`, and `requirements.txt`), detect the MCP and local-AI signals from declared dependency or configuration entry names. A normalized entry named exactly `mcp` must produce the `manifest_entries` value `mcp`; one named exactly `ollama` must produce the `dependencies` value `ollama`.

Do not produce either signal merely because those words appear elsewhere in a manifest, including comments, descriptive metadata, or longer dependency names such as `mcp-tools` and `ollama-client`. Preserve the existing evidence basis and category-pack behavior.
acceptance_test_source:
from __future__ import annotations

import pytest

from gitseed.category import FileEvidenceReader
from gitseed.collect.search import Candidate
from gitseed.pipeline.run import FetchedFiles


CANDIDATE = Candidate("owner/repo", "owner", "", 0, "")


VALID_MANIFESTS = (
    ("package.json", '{"dependencies": {"mcp": "1.0", "ollama": "1.0"}}'),
    ("pyproject.toml", '[project]\ndependencies = ["mcp>=1", "ollama>=1"]\n'),
    ("Cargo.toml", '[dependencies]\nmcp = "1"\nollama = "1"\n'),
    (
        "go.mod",
        "module example.invalid/project\n\nrequire (\n    example.invalid/mcp v1.0.0\n    example.invalid/ollama v1.0.0\n)\n",
    ),
    ("requirements.txt", "mcp==1.0\nollama==1.0\n"),
)


NEAR_MISS_MANIFESTS = (
    (
        "package.json",
        '{"description": "MCP and Ollama are mentioned only in prose", '
        '"dependencies": {"mcp-tools": "1.0", "ollama-client": "1.0"}}',
    ),
    (
        "pyproject.toml",
        "# MCP and Ollama are not dependencies here\n"
        "[project]\n"
        'dependencies = ["mcp-tools>=1", "ollama-client>=1"]\n',
    ),
    (
        "Cargo.toml",
        "# MCP and Ollama are not dependencies here\n"
        "[dependencies]\n"
        'mcp-tools = "1"\n'
        'ollama-client = "1"\n',
    ),
    (
        "go.mod",
        "// MCP and Ollama are not dependencies here\n"
        "module example.invalid/project\n\n"
        "require (\n"
        "    example.invalid/mcp-tools v1.0.0\n"
        "    example.invalid/ollama-client v1.0.0\n"
        ")\n",
    ),
    (
        "requirements.txt",
        "# MCP and Ollama are not dependencies here\n"
        "mcp-tools==1.0\n"
        "ollama-client==1.0\n",
    ),
)


def _evidence_values(path: str, text: str) -> dict[str, frozenset[str]]:
    evidence = FileEvidenceReader().read_evidence(
        CANDIDATE,
        FetchedFiles(((path, text),)),
        None,
    )
    return {item.evidence: item.values for item in evidence}


@pytest.mark.parametrize(("path", "text"), VALID_MANIFESTS)
def test_declared_manifest_dependencies_produce_category_evidence(
    path: str, text: str
) -> None:
    values = _evidence_values(path, text)

    assert values["manifest_entries"] == frozenset({"mcp"})
    assert values["dependencies"] == frozenset({"ollama"})


@pytest.mark.parametrize(("path", "text"), NEAR_MISS_MANIFESTS)
def test_manifest_prose_comments_and_longer_package_names_do_not_produce_category_evidence(
    path: str, text: str
) -> None:
    values = _evidence_values(path, text)

    assert values["manifest_entries"] == frozenset()
    assert values["dependencies"] == frozenset()
why_it_fails_on_the_current_tree: `FileEvidenceReader` concatenates each supported manifest's raw lowercase text and uses substring containment. Every near-miss fixture therefore incorrectly emits both signals because its comments, prose, or longer package names contain `mcp` and `ollama`.
two_different_implementations_that_would: Use format-aware readers to obtain dependency/configuration names, canonicalize those names, and compare them to the two signal names.
Use independent extractors for each supported manifest syntax that expose only declared dependency/configuration identifiers before applying the same exact-name checks.
